trial_court: VI Additional Principal Judge, Family Court, Bengaluru, M.C No.2089/2005 and M.C No.279/2004
case_name: K R Prasad vs Smt. B S Lakshmi
outcome_detected: In the result the same are dismissed
facts_of_case: The parties are K R Prasad and Smt. B S Lakshmi. The husband filed a petition under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act for restitution of conjugal rights, which was allowed by the trial court. The wife filed a petition under Section 13(i), 1(a) and 13(ib) of the Hindu Marriage Act for dissolution of marriage, which was rejected by the trial court.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party seeking restitution of conjugal rights to prove that there has been no reasonable cohabitation for a period of three years.
legal_principles.held: It is held that the burden lies on the party seeking restitution of conjugal rights to prove that there has been no reasonable cohabitation for a period of three years.

legal_principles.principle: The court will not interfere with the amicable settlement arrived at between the parties unless it is contrary to public policy or statute.
legal_principles.held: This Court will not interfere with the amicable settlement arrived at between the parties unless it is contrary to public policy or statute.

outcome.final_order: The appeals are dismissed. The parties have amicably resolved their dispute and arrived at an agreement under Section 89 of the Code of Civil Procedure.
